interfaces.name: Covariance matrix
interfaces.type_shape: Covariance of the zero-mean population vector. This is not the sample covariance or the covariance of the contaminated observations.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Covariance of the zero-mean population vector. This is not the sample covariance or the covariance of the contaminated observations.

members.statement_original: In this paper, we are interested in estimating the covariance matrix $\Sigma=\mathbb E[XX^\top]$ of a random vector $X\in\mathbb R^d$ with zero mean from independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) copies $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ of $X$.

interfaces.name: I.i.d. sample with contamination
interfaces.type_shape: Original complete assumption: iid clean observations, finite p-th norm moment for p>=4, zero mean, nonzero covariance, standardized moment constant and bounded replacements. Y need not be iid or independent of X.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Original complete assumption: iid clean observations, finite p-th norm moment for p>=4, zero mean, nonzero covariance, standardized moment constant and bounded replacements. Y need not be iid or independent of X.

members.statement_original:
$X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are i.i.d. copies of a random element $X$ of $\mathbb R^d$ satisfying $\mathbb E[\|X\|^p]<+\infty$ for some $p\geq4$. We assume $\mathbb E[X]=0$, that the covariance $\Sigma$ of $X$ is non-null, and set
\[
\kappa_p:=\sup_{v\in\mathbb R^d,\,\langle v,\Sigma v\rangle=1}\mathbb E[|\langle X,v\rangle|^p]^{\frac1p}.
\]
Finally, we let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n$ denote other random elements of $\mathbb R^d$ that satisfy the following condition:
\[
\#\{i\in[n]:Y_i\ne X_i\}\leq\eta n
\]
for some $\eta\in[0,1)$.

interfaces.name: Moment condition
interfaces.type_shape: The displayed definition is kappa_p, whereas the adjacent text calls its square the hypercontractivity constant. Kappa_4 in the theorem is this moment definition at exponent four. The direction is normalized by population variance, not Euclidean length.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: The displayed definition is kappa_p, whereas the adjacent text calls its square the hypercontractivity constant. Kappa_4 in the theorem is this moment definition at exponent four. The direction is normalized by population variance, not Euclidean length.

naming_context.text: The sole requirement is that the one-dimensional marginals satisfy a moment condition, $\kappa_p^2$ is referred to as the $L^p-L^2$ hypercontractivity constant by [Abdalla and Zhivotovskiy, 2022] and elsewhere in the literature.

interfaces.name: Stable rank
interfaces.type_shape: Trace divided by operator norm for a nonzero symmetric positive semidefinite matrix. In the theorem M=Sigma; this is neither algebraic rank nor the squared Frobenius-to-operator ratio sometimes given the same name.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Trace divided by operator norm for a nonzero symmetric positive semidefinite matrix. In the theorem M=Sigma; this is neither algebraic rank nor the squared Frobenius-to-operator ratio sometimes given the same name.

members.statement_original:
The stable rank of a non-zero matrix $M\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}_{\geq0}$ is given by:
\[
r(M)=\frac{\operatorname{tr}(M)}{\|M\|}.
\]
